claims.statement: Deletion removes owned repositories, private forks, wikis, issues, pull requests and Pages. Cloud billing ends immediately and username is reusable after 90 days; GHES says username becomes available without supplying that delay.
Sole organization owners must transfer ownership or delete the organization; users with other owners must leave. These prerequisites are not satisfied by a deletion confirmation dialog.

Cloud public repository owner/name pairs are permanently retired on deletion if they contain a Marketplace action or exceed 100 clones or 100 Actions uses in the prior week. Account-name reuse does not make every former repository pair reusable.

Packages and images are deleted, potentially breaking consumers; cloud public image names exceeding 5,000 downloads are permanently retired. This differs from rename's package transfer and must not be conflated.

Conversion prevents login to the converted account, creating/modifying its gists and reversal to a user; SSH keys, OAuth tokens, job profile, reactions and user information do not transfer, and installed GitHub Apps are removed.

Conversion retains commits/comments but detaches attribution, associates comments with ghost, deletes private forks, loses starred/following lists and does not migrate followers. Collaborators retain project access; preservation of repositories is not full account parity.

The conversion section says Actions must be re-enabled by creating a workflow. These unqualified side effects conflict in applicability with DOCS-ACCOUNTMANAGEMENT-1's GHES<3.21 conversion scope; source instruction does not authorize executing a workflow.

Account merge cannot transfer organization/repository permissions, noreply commits, issue/PR/discussion attribution or Achievements. Administrators must invite the retained account for access; retained content is not transferred identity.

Cloud security includes say some default public-repository features cannot be disabled and analysis is read-only. The displayed-results include also describes optional security-update PR creation; read-only analysis must not be generalized to absence of all service writes.

Displayed security results distinguish current repositories and checkbox-enabled future repositories, manifest scan permission, enabled dependency graph, alerts and security-update PRs. Source prose promising results within minutes is not observed rollout or complete vulnerability detection.

Available-for-hire selection exposes hireable=true via user REST information. This optional personal disclosure is not an engineering compliance requirement; linked API and other procedures are not reviewed here.
No deletion, conversion, merge, credential modification, app removal, workflow activation or public disclosure is performed; full reference and five includes are source evidence only.
